scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): backs long-term goals while granting that a healthy wish for recognition can help; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose at about 400 words on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: Countless young people today dream of becoming famous quickly, often overnight.
Some people recommend that young people should be encouraged to pursue long-term, realistic goals rather than seek immediate fame and recognition.
I largely agree that long-term goals are wiser, though I believe a desire for recognition is not always harmful.

sections.role: Body 1 — Why long-term goals are wiser

sentences.text: First, long-term, realistic goals usually lead to deeper and more lasting success.
Steady effort toward a clear goal builds real skills that cannot be gained overnight.
For example, a young person who trains patiently for years to become a doctor gains both security and genuine respect.
This shows that worthwhile achievements almost always require time, patience, and hard work.
Chasing instant fame, by contrast, often ends in disappointment when the attention quickly fades.
Many people who become famous suddenly are forgotten just as fast, left with nothing solid behind them.
For these reasons, encouraging realistic long-term goals is wise advice for the young.

sections.role: Body 2 — Why recognition is not always bad

sentences.text: Second, however, the wish for recognition is not always something to discourage.
A healthy desire for praise can motivate young people to work hard and to aim high.
Consider a young scientist whose hope of being recognised pushes her to make a real and lasting discovery.
Such ambition shows that recognition and long-term goals can support each other rather than conflict.
The danger lies not in wanting recognition but in wanting it instantly and without effort.
Some early encouragement and attention can even give young people the confidence to pursue bigger goals.
Recognition, then, becomes harmful only when it replaces patience and real achievement.
In conclusion, young people are wise to pursue long-term, realistic goals rather than chase quick fame.
But a reasonable wish for recognition can itself encourage the effort that those goals demand.
The best advice is to aim for lasting achievement while letting a healthy hope for recognition fuel the journey.
